history.p: Gade's seventh symphony was written during the Second Schleswig War in 1864, which however did not affect his music. In a letter to his sister-in-law, Frederikke Christensen, he wrote: "this summer my muse has bestowed upon me a new symphony - and what is gratifying: a fresh and cheeky one. It does neither deal with war nor with peace stories and even less with politics, but I am sure that you will find it interesting to listen to".

physDesc.physMedium: 7 bifolios, 6 single folios and a scrap of paper (title page). Written in ink. Paper: 16 staves (first movement) and 18 staves (second and third movements). Numerous corrections and cancellations in ink and red and blue pencil. Several pages are discarded and replaced by a new version in piano score. The notation of some of the sections in the third movement is very rudimentary.

Paginated 1-42 (first and second movement); 1-33 (third movement); and 1-33 (fourth movement). Heading on p. 1: "Symphonie / No 7." In upper right-hand corner "Niels W: Gade /Op 45.". first movement dated "29 August 64. / [Gade's musical signature];"second movement dated "[Gade's musical signature] Sept. 64."; after the third movement: "Fine G.B. 25/2 65."; fourth movement dated: "Fine / Septbr. 1864 [Gade' musical signature] / S.D.G.".

annot.p: The autograph score of the third movement is lost. It was probably still in Leipzig with Breitkopf & Härtel, when Gade wanted to perform the symphony on 9 March 1865. Therefore Gade asked the composer, organist and music teacher Georg Carl Bohlmann, who also instrumentated some of J.P.E. Hartmann's later works, to prepare a new score on basis of his sketches.
